edges.description: Dysplastic epithelial cells can line a fistula in the setting of fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma, but the case observation does not determine the directness or timing of the inflammation-to-dysplasia transition.
Dysplastic fistula lining and proliferating mucinous adenocarcinoma were observed together along the same tract, but a single case cannot establish the direct clonal transition.
Anorectal fistula cancer can extend into multiple pelvic structures, but the available case reports do not resolve the mechanistic steps from local mucinous growth to widespread invasion.
A fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma case presented with progressive anal pain and a palpable tumor, although the report does not isolate the causal contribution of tumor growth to pain.
Locally advanced anorectal fistula cancer can cause anal stenosis through a pelvic mass.

Local anal or anorectal tumor burden may be accompanied by rectal bleeding or serosanguineous discharge. The cited report supports the symptom association but explicitly cannot exclude a low rectal primary, so this link is partial and its directness is unresolved.
edges.target: Rectal bleeding or serosanguineous anal discharge

edges.description: The anal gland/transitional subtype is associated with higher PD-1/PD-L1 expression than the colorectal-type subtype; the cohort does not establish a causal direction from subtype identity to checkpoint expression.

nodes.description: Persistent perianal abscess and anal fistula create a chronic inflammatory epithelial-tract context implicated in fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma. The available evidence is case-level and does not establish how long inflammation must persist before epithelial change occurs.

evidence.snippet: A long-standing (over 10 years) anal fistula is considered a fundamental cause of fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma (FAMC).

nodes.description: Poorly differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma can proliferate through the dermis and epidermis at the distal aspect of an anal fistula. Separate case-level evidence shows that anorectal fistula cancer can also present with widespread pelvic infiltration.

evidence.reference_title: A case report of anal fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma developing 3 years after treatment of perianal abscess.
evidence.snippet: Histopathology showed highly dysplastic cells lining the lumen of the anal fistula and poorly differentiated mucinous adenocarcinoma proliferating in the dermis and epidermis in the distal aspect of the fistula.

nodes.description: Highly dysplastic epithelial cells can line the lumen of an anal fistula adjacent to fistula-associated mucinous adenocarcinoma. This is a histopathologic precursor context rather than proof of a clonal precursor relationship in every tumor.

nodes.description: Locally advanced anorectal fistula cancer can infiltrate the prostate, seminal vesicles, levator ani, and obturator musculature, producing a large pelvic tumor burden. This evidence comes from an individual Crohn disease-associated case.

nodes.description: The anal gland/transitional-type subset has higher PD-1/PD-L1 expression and a different tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte profile than colorectal-type tumors, creating a biologic rationale for immune-checkpoint-directed clinical research while not establishing prospective efficacy for this rare tumor.

evidence.reference_title: A dualistic model of primary anal canal adenocarcinoma with distinct cellular origins, etiologies, inflammatory microenvironments and mutational signatures: implications for personalised medicine.
evidence.snippet: anal gland/transitional-type cancers, which poorly respond to standard treatments, displayed less mutations in downstream effectors of the EGFR signalling pathway (i.e., KRAS and NRAS) and demonstrated a significantly higher expression of the immune inhibitory ligand-receptor pair PD-1/PD-L1 compared to their counterparts arising from the colorectal mucosa.

evidence.snippet: This case highlights the challenges of early diagnosis of anal malignancies and the importance of prompt evaluation of anorectal area by anoscopy and colonoscopy if symptoms of rectal bleeding or serosanguinous anal discharge are reported.

nodes.description: A molecular cohort separated primary anal canal adenocarcinoma into two region-specific entities that differ in HPV status, immune contexture, checkpoint expression, and mutation profile. This node records subtype context and association rather than asserting a causal sequence between those features.
